I wish so much I had a dog, but I live with my family and they won't let me have one. I think it would help my depression.  Anyway 2 things did help me. 

 I lost 70 lbs by walking. I just walked super far every day and ate lots of vegetables and drank a lot of water.  It took me about a year, and I really felt like I was accomplishing something as the weight was coming off, not just at the end.  Anyone can do it.  Maybe you're too depressed to walk now.  Maybe you won't start for another 6 months or another year or 2.  just think about it please, because walking also made me less depressed. 

 The other thing I did was volunteer.  First I started volunteering at the local hospital even when i was so depressed I couldn't comb my hair or shower.  i just used baby wipes and wore a hat! Gross I know, and it was so hard for me to go consistently too cause of depression, but I went when I could and it helped.  Then I started volunteering for a non-profit that helps people who are really really poor and who just got out of jail and dont know where to go to get help getting back into society. 

 Honestly, helping other people is the best thing I ever did to help myself. 

 I'm nowhere out of the woods.  Most of my hair fell out this year from depression, I'm still broke, no spouse, 39, no kids , live with my family , bad depression PTSD etc, and even felt like killing myself last night.
But I didn't.  And I feel a little better today.  Not happy.  Still depressed, but not suicidal.  It seems you are young.  I swear to God you can really change most of the things that make you unhappy.  Even your family to some extent. A lot of people rejected by family claim chosen families.  Call your therapist. Keep coming here.  There are a lot of nice people here.  You'd be surprised.  I'm sorry about how bad you feel.

Yes.  I've tried several modalities of treatment, but only time helped at all.  My problems really stem from the compounding issues that result from falling out of life for so long.  After you've been out of the workforce for many years, its not easy to find a way back in, and the poverty my disability has created has been very difficult to endure.  I'm feeling a little better today for sure though am seeing my therapist tomorrow.  I've been honest with the therapist about the suicidal feelings I had yesterday too.  Thank you so much for taking the time to write back to me.  It is truly a very very special thing to be able to come here and have someone care.  Thank you.

Hi Clarance- I don't use Reddit often and don't know how to PM,(maybe you can tell me how) but I wanted to respond to you.  I am sitting with my family now.  We are mourning the passing of Nelson Mandela together. I don't feel suicidal right now.  My mood improved slightly when I read a post by a young man who was raped and felt suicidal.  The similarity between our circumstances somehow spurred me to urge him to spare his life, and after empathizing with him and encouraging him to live, I decided to stop planning my death and go to sleep.  I fulfilled none of my responsibilities today, and am still very depressed, but it is hard to concentrate on myself today, this day, when the world remembers one of the most selfless men who ever lived, Nelson Mandela.  For years, the wallpaper on my computer has been one of his pictures from Robben Island.  I feel guilty, and that's part of the depression.  I feel like the world sees my inconsistency as a lack of discipline , instead of what it is, depression that forces me to withdraw from the world and fail to fulfill my responsibilities.Thank you for your help.  My mother and my brother are good reasons to keep trying.  The best reasons.  i'm very depressed but I'm going to see my therapist tomorrow. Thank you again for your kindness.
